## Diagnosis
It is past fine in its exhibits and still merely fine in its connective prose: the deck, the henhouse, the laptop, the plumber's form, the one chair the consequences cannot reach — those hold, and nothing needs adding to them. What holds the piece back now is the sentence that follows the object and restates it in the register the essay is prosecuting, most damagingly in the risk paragraph, which shifts a hazard onto "whoever executes" while the surrounding pages are convicting other writers for exactly that dodge. A smaller symptom of the same slackness: "the oldest in business" at the third question and "the oldest move in business" nine paragraphs later, a formula the piece spends twice and earns once.

## Suggestions
### 1
Original: I have not met the man, and a picture of him is not the same as a man understood.
Replacement: I have not met the man, and this picture of him is a guess.
Buys: Removes an aphorism-shaped clause from the last position before the locked close, and fixes the pronoun, which currently refers to a picture rather than to the guess.

### 2
Original: Theater remains, because a chatbot and the right vocabulary keep up appearances.
Replacement: Theater remains, because a chatbot and the right vocabulary cost less than the people who could answer the questions.
Buys: Ends the section on the trade the restructuring actually made instead of a stock phrase, and closes the loop with the expensive seniors two sentences earlier.

### 3
Original: A document that raises the risk and names no mitigation does not remove the risk; it merely shifts it onto whoever executes.
Replacement: A document that raises the risk and names no mitigation does not remove the risk; it hands the risk to the people who will be in the room when the number does not arrive.
Buys: Puts bodies where the sentence currently has a passive shadow, and stops the essay from committing the agentless dodge it catalogues.

### 4
Original: Ten years have found me responsible for AI strategy in production systems, which mostly means I am the one who must state what a plan will cost and who will actually pay for it, and I write every article with AI assistance, spending hours each week extracting prose that looks finished from these models.
Replacement: For ten years I have been responsible for AI strategy in production systems, which mostly means I am the one who has to say what a plan will cost and who will pay for it. I also draft every article with these models, hours a week spent pulling prose that looks finished out of them.
Buys: Two receipts stop competing inside one 60-word sentence, and "Ten years have found me" stops sounding like a memoir opening.

### 5
Original: Trying to size a business that does not exist reveals nothing about whether it will ever exist.
Replacement: CUT
Buys: The sentence circles back on its own terms; the money-moving-past line before it has already landed and is weakened by the follow-up.

### 6
Original: The difference between a real strategy and a document that looks like one depends on three questions: what are we building, who is going to buy it, and how much money are we going to make.
Replacement: Three questions separate a strategy from a document that looks like one: what are we building, who is going to buy it, and how much money are we going to make.
Buys: Drops a banned intensifier and a limp verb; the questions do the separating instead of a difference depending on them.

## Paragraph move
Move the three-sentence paragraph beginning "An argument makes a claim that could be wrong" up to sit immediately after the Figure 1 caption, where the picture has just shown a sentence that can be proven wrong beside one that cannot. The definition currently arrives eighteen paragraphs late, as abstraction the figure already made visible; placed against the figure it reads as a caption to an object, and its departure lets the alibi paragraph run straight into Orwell's henhouse.
